newsitem.title: UK: IRA warns of no let-up in anti-British violence.
newsitem.headline: IRA warns of no let-up in anti-British violence.

text.p: IRA guerrillas said on Wednesday they would continue an armed campaign against British rule over Northern Ireland, but made no reference to two suspected IRA bombs in northwestern England.

In a hardline statement the Irish Republican Army leadership blamed Britain for the breakdown of a 17-month truce in February 1996 and said London's refusal to bring Sinn Fein, its political arm, into talks was holding up a resolution of the conflict.
"In the period since (the truce breakdown) we have demonstrated again and again that we retain the capacity and resources to continue to strike against those maintaining British occupation.
"Everyone should be assured that we are united, we are strong and we remain steadfast in our determination to achieve our objectives."
The statement made no reference to the bombings in the town of Wilmslow early on Wednesday which damaged rail tracks.

Issued in the form of an annual "Easter Message" to coincide with republican commemorations this weekend of the IRA's Dublin rebellion against British rule in 1916, it said Britain had shown it was not committed to building a peace process.
Britain, backed by Ireland, says Sinn Fein will not get a seat in multi-party talks about the province's future until the guerrillas abandon violence to prove commitment to democracy.

"We have repeated often in the past and do so again today that we stand ready to face our responsibilities in facilitating a process aimed at securing a lasting resolution to the conflict between the British government and the Irish people....

"Their refusal to make such a commitment and their futile pursuit of an IRA defeat serves no other end than the postponement of both lasting peace and the date of British withdrawal. We remain determined to bring that date forward."
The conflict in Northern Ireland has cost more than 3,200 lives over 28 years. Tension has risen after the IRA killed two soldiers in bomb and gun attacks since last October.
A truce by Protestant Loyalist guerrillas, who support rule from London, is unstable and Loyalists have been blamed for murdering a Catholic two weeks ago.
